minutes.headline: Planning Board backed pursuing state technical-assistance funding for MBTA zoning, heard water bylaw compromise talks, kept the pledge.
minutes.summary: The board heard a Montachusett Regional Planning Commission presentation on MBTA Communities multifamily zoning for Lunenburg and agreed to pursue Mass Housing Partnership technical assistance funding. It held a long joint discussion with the Water Commissioners on the water supply protection district bylaw (Zone 1, 2 and 3 uses, special permit versus site plan approval), with no decision. It continued the Sunny Hill Road stormwater hearing, cancelled the Lancaster signage hearing, granted a certificate of completion for 321 Sunny Hill Road, and voted by show of hands to keep saying the Pledge.

public_comment.topic: Chair opened public comment at the start of the meeting; none offered.
Joan P., Winter Green Court, said residents have no objection to removing section E (farming, gardening) from Zone 1 uses.

Joan P. said residents are not opposed to treatment plants but want a special permit for new ones in Zones 2 and 3 so neighbors can have input on screening and placement; said the bylaw failed at town meeting before.
Asked whether industrial versus residential areas are treated differently and who looks out for the neighborhood.
Argued only water district voters vote before a project reaches the board, so a special permit should stay in the board's back pocket.
Said voters want the most stringent regulation and a special permit is the way to get two-thirds at town meeting.
Proposed compromise: no treatment plant in Zone 1 within 400 feet of a lake shore; later proposed special permit for any new construction in Zones 1 and 2.
Remote member of the public asked why saying the Pledge is so important to those who want it.
Thanked the board for the pledge vote and criticized chair comments about attracting attendance.

budget_items.what_was_said: The prior planning assistance grant for the MBTA work ended June 30, so more technical assistance is needed.
Options are another planning assistance grant, the District Local Technical Assistance next January, or Mass Housing Partnership funding with a 4 to 8 month timeframe.
Noncompliance with MBTA zoning could make the town ineligible for Housing Choice, Green Communities, MassWorks and other grants.
A guarantee covers 317 and 321 Sunny Hill and remains if the certificate is issued.
Water district said treatment plants are very costly and forcing them out of the protection zones would add millions.

budget_items.topic: Water treatment design and construction cost
budget_items.what_was_said: Design alone and the full facility were estimated by the water superintendent, requiring district votes.
Applicant said he had not yet paid the application fee and abutters list steps.

decisions.decision: Board agreed to pursue Mass Housing Partnership technical assistance for MBTA zoning; Mr. Harris to review the MHP application and draft it for the town manager's signature.
Chapman to send MHP information; a support letter could be obtained from the town manager for the planning assistance grant due July 22nd.
Mr. Harris will revise the water protection bylaw draft including the special permit for Zones 1 and 2 option for the August 26th discussion.
Public hearing on the water bylaw tentatively aimed for September 23rd, not yet scheduled.
Board and water district agreed to remove section E (farming/gardening) from Zone 1 permitted uses.
Water commissioners to discuss the special permit compromise at their Wednesday meeting and report back to the board.
Signage applicant to email staff to withdraw without prejudice and resubmit a complete application later.
Chair asked members to email conflicts for July 22nd; new member would not vote on the Sunny Hill hearing as he was not on the board when it started.
May 13 and June 12/10 minutes not approved; Mr. Harris to review and send comments; minutes to be corrected and brought back.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted to pursue Mass Housing Partnership technical assistance funding to evaluate MBTA Communities zoning compliance.
A long joint session with the Water Commissioners on the water supply protection district bylaw ended with no decision; a redraft is due for August 26th.
The board and the water district agreed to remove farming and gardening (section E) from the Zone 1 permitted uses.
The Sunny Hill Road stormwater hearing was continued to July 22nd, and a certificate of completion was granted for 321 Sunny Hill Road.
The Lancaster signage hearing was cancelled so the applicant can withdraw and resubmit, and a show of hands favored keeping the Pledge of Allegiance.

why_it_matters: Noncompliance with MBTA zoning could make the town ineligible for grants such as Housing Choice, Green Communities and MassWorks, so the technical-assistance application bears on future town funding and on a zoning article residents may be asked to vote on.

The water bylaw failed at town meeting before, and whether new treatment plants in the protection zones need a special permit is still open, so the final wording will decide what residents are asked to approve.
watch_next: July 22nd: the Mass Housing Partnership application and support letter are due, and the Sunny Hill Road stormwater hearing resumes at 6:05 p.m.
August 26th: the revised water bylaw draft, with the special permit option for Zones 1 and 2, returns for discussion; a public hearing is tentatively aimed at September 23rd.
